requirement.text: The infusion pump software shall implement a rate-limiting algorithm that constrains the commanded flow rate to a maximum of 1200 mL/hr and a minimum of 0.1 mL/hr, with a resolution of 0.1 mL/hr increments.

test_cases.description: Verify rate-limiting algorithm accepts valid flow rates within the specified range.
test_cases.setup: Infusion pump software build v3.2.1 deployed in test environment; rate-control module initialized; hardware motor driver in simulation mode.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Command flow rate of 100.0 mL/hr via the rate-control API.
Step: 2. Verify the commanded rate is accepted and applied to the motor driver.
Step: 3. Command flow rate of 0.5 mL/hr.
Step: 4. Verify the commanded rate is accepted and applied.
Step: 5. Command flow rate of 1200.0 mL/hr.
Step: 6. Verify the commanded rate is accepted and applied.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Rate-control module accepts 100.0 mL/hr without error.
ExpectedResult: 2. Motor driver receives pulse timing corresponding to 100.0 mL/hr.
ExpectedResult: 3. Rate-control module accepts 0.5 mL/hr without error.
ExpectedResult: 4. Motor driver receives pulse timing corresponding to 0.5 mL/hr.
ExpectedResult: 5. Rate-control module accepts 1200.0 mL/hr without error.
ExpectedResult: 6. Motor driver receives pulse timing corresponding to 1200.0 mL/hr.

test_cases.description: Verify rate-limiting algorithm rejects flow rates below the minimum threshold.
test_cases.setup: Infusion pump software build v3.2.1 deployed in test environment; rate-control module initialized.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Command flow rate of 0.05 mL/hr (below minimum).
Step: 2. Observe the rate-control module response.
Step: 3. Verify the motor driver state remains unchanged.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Rate-control module rejects the command with error code ERR_RATE_BELOW_MIN.
ExpectedResult: 2. Error message states 'Flow rate 0.05 mL/hr is below minimum 0.1 mL/hr'.
ExpectedResult: 3. Motor driver pulse timing remains at the previously commanded rate.

test_cases.description: Verify rate-limiting algorithm rejects flow rates above the maximum threshold.
test_cases.setup: Infusion pump software build v3.2.1 deployed in test environment; rate-control module initialized.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Command flow rate of 1200.1 mL/hr (above maximum).
Step: 2. Observe the rate-control module response.
Step: 3. Verify the motor driver state remains unchanged.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Rate-control module rejects the command with error code ERR_RATE_ABOVE_MAX.
ExpectedResult: 2. Error message states 'Flow rate 1200.1 mL/hr exceeds maximum 1200.0 mL/hr'.
ExpectedResult: 3. Motor driver pulse timing remains at the previously commanded rate.

test_cases.description: Verify rate-limiting algorithm enforces 0.1 mL/hr resolution.
test_cases.setup: Infusion pump software build v3.2.1 deployed in test environment; rate-control module initialized.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Command flow rate of 50.15 mL/hr (invalid resolution).
Step: 2. Observe the rate-control module response.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Rate-control module rejects the command with error code ERR_RATE_INVALID_RESOLUTION.
ExpectedResult: 2. Error message states 'Flow rate must be specified in 0.1 mL/hr increments'.

design_docs.name: Rate Limiting Algorithm Design
design_docs.description: Describes the PID controller implementation, saturation limits, and anti-windup logic for the rate-limiting control loop. Specifies the input validation logic that enforces minimum (0.1 mL/hr), maximum (1200.0 mL/hr), and resolution (0.1 mL/hr increments) constraints before commanding the motor driver.

design_docs.name: Motor Driver Interface Design
design_docs.description: Specifies the hardware abstraction layer for motor control signals, pulse timing constraints, and safe-state latch behavior. Documents the pulse-width modulation (PWM) frequency and duty cycle calculations that translate commanded flow rates into motor driver signals.

design_docs.name: Rate Control Software Detailed Design
design_docs.description: Detailed design of the rate-control task, including the state machine for rate transitions, error handling for invalid commands, and the watchdog heartbeat protocol that monitors the control loop for stalls or hangs.

requirement.text: The EHR system shall enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all users accessing patient health information (PHI), requiring both a password and a time-based one-time password (TOTP) token generated by an authenticator app.

test_cases.description: Verify successful login with valid password and valid TOTP token.
test_cases.setup: EHR authentication service running; test user account provisioned with TOTP secret; authenticator app synchronized.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to EHR login page.
Step: 2. Enter valid username and password.
Step: 3. Submit credentials.
Step: 4. Observe MFA prompt.
Step: 5. Generate current TOTP token from authenticator app.
Step: 6. Enter TOTP token.
Step: 7. Submit MFA form.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Login page loads successfully.
ExpectedResult: 2. Credentials are accepted.
ExpectedResult: 3. System redirects to MFA prompt page.
ExpectedResult: 4. MFA prompt displays 'Enter your 6-digit authentication code'.
ExpectedResult: 5. TOTP token is generated (e.g., 123456).
ExpectedResult: 6. TOTP token is accepted.
ExpectedResult: 7. User is authenticated and redirected to EHR dashboard.

test_cases.description: Verify login is denied when valid password is provided but TOTP token is invalid.
test_cases.setup: EHR authentication service running; test user account provisioned with TOTP secret.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to EHR login page.
Step: 2. Enter valid username and password.
Step: 3. Submit credentials.
Step: 4. Enter invalid TOTP token (e.g., 000000).
Step: 5. Submit MFA form.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Credentials are accepted and MFA prompt is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. System rejects the invalid TOTP token.
ExpectedResult: 3. Error message displays 'Invalid authentication code. Please try again.'
ExpectedResult: 4. User remains on MFA prompt page and is not authenticated.

test_cases.description: Verify login is denied when password is invalid, regardless of TOTP token validity.
test_cases.setup: EHR authentication service running; test user account provisioned.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to EHR login page.
Step: 2. Enter valid username and invalid password.
Step: 3. Submit credentials.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. System rejects the credentials.
ExpectedResult: 2. Error message displays 'Invalid username or password'.
ExpectedResult: 3. User remains on login page and MFA prompt is never displayed.

test_cases.description: Verify MFA enforcement cannot be bypassed by direct URL navigation.
test_cases.setup: EHR authentication service running; test user has valid credentials but has not completed MFA.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Complete first-factor authentication (password only).
Step: 2. Capture the session token from browser cookies.
Step: 3. Attempt to navigate directly to the EHR dashboard URL without completing MFA.
Step: 4. Observe the system response.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Password authentication succeeds and MFA prompt is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. Session token is captured but marked as 'MFA_PENDING'.
ExpectedResult: 3. System intercepts the direct navigation attempt.
ExpectedResult: 4. User is redirected back to the MFA prompt page with message 'Multi-factor authentication required'.

design_docs.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Architecture
design_docs.description: Describes the two-phase authentication flow: first-factor (password) validation against the user database, followed by second-factor (TOTP) validation using the HMAC-based One-Time Password algorithm (RFC 6238). Documents the session state machine that tracks MFA completion status and prevents bypass via direct URL navigation.

design_docs.name: TOTP Token Validation Interface Design
design_docs.description: Specifies the TOTP validation service interface, including the time-window tolerance (±1 time step, 30 seconds), the HMAC-SHA1 algorithm implementation, and the secret key storage and retrieval mechanisms from the secure credential vault.

design_docs.name: Session Management Detailed Design
design_docs.description: Detailed design of the session token lifecycle, including the MFA_PENDING state that is set after first-factor authentication and cleared only after successful TOTP validation. Documents the middleware that intercepts all PHI-accessing routes and enforces MFA completion before granting access.

requirement.text: The telemedicine video consultation module shall automatically degrade the video stream quality from HD (1280x720) to SD (640x480) when the detected network bandwidth drops below 1.5 Mbps, and shall restore HD quality when bandwidth recovers above 2.0 Mbps for at least 10 consecutive seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify video quality degrades to SD when bandwidth drops below 1.5 Mbps.
test_cases.setup: Telemedicine video module active; provider and patient connected in HD video call; network throttling tool configured.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Establish HD video call between provider and patient.
Step: 2. Verify current video resolution is 1280x720.
Step: 3. Throttle network bandwidth to 1.2 Mbps.
Step: 4. Observe video stream quality and resolution.
Step: 5. Verify UI notification is displayed.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Video call establishes successfully in HD mode.
ExpectedResult: 2. Video resolution is confirmed as 1280x720 via WebRTC stats API.
ExpectedResult: 3. Bandwidth drops below 1.5 Mbps threshold.
ExpectedResult: 4. Video stream automatically degrades to 640x480 resolution within 3 seconds.
ExpectedResult: 5. UI displays toast notification 'Video quality reduced due to low bandwidth'.

test_cases.description: Verify video quality restores to HD when bandwidth recovers above 2.0 Mbps for 10 seconds.
test_cases.setup: Telemedicine video module active; video call currently in SD mode due to previous bandwidth degradation; network throttling tool configured.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Verify current video resolution is 640x480 (SD mode).
Step: 2. Increase network bandwidth to 2.5 Mbps.
Step: 3. Maintain bandwidth at 2.5 Mbps for 10 seconds.
Step: 4. Observe video stream quality and resolution.
Step: 5. Verify UI notification is displayed.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Video resolution is confirmed as 640x480 via WebRTC stats API.
ExpectedResult: 2. Bandwidth increases above 2.0 Mbps threshold.
ExpectedResult: 3. Bandwidth remains stable above 2.0 Mbps for 10 consecutive seconds.
ExpectedResult: 4. Video stream automatically upgrades to 1280x720 resolution.
ExpectedResult: 5. UI displays toast notification 'Video quality restored to HD'.

test_cases.description: Verify video quality does NOT restore to HD if bandwidth drops below 2.0 Mbps before 10-second stabilization period completes.
test_cases.setup: Telemedicine video module active; video call in SD mode; network throttling tool configured.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Verify current video resolution is 640x480.
Step: 2. Increase bandwidth to 2.5 Mbps.
Step: 3. After 5 seconds, drop bandwidth to 1.8 Mbps.
Step: 4. Observe video stream quality.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Video resolution is 640x480.
ExpectedResult: 2. Bandwidth increases above 2.0 Mbps.
ExpectedResult: 3. Bandwidth drops below 2.0 Mbps before 10-second timer completes.
ExpectedResult: 4. Video stream remains in SD mode (640x480); no upgrade to HD occurs.

test_cases.description: Verify video quality degradation boundary at exactly 1.5 Mbps.
test_cases.setup: Telemedicine video module active; HD video call established; network throttling tool configured.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Establish HD video call.
Step: 2. Throttle bandwidth to exactly 1.5 Mbps.
Step: 3. Observe video stream quality for 10 seconds.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Video call is in HD mode (1280x720).
ExpectedResult: 2. Bandwidth is exactly at the 1.5 Mbps threshold.
ExpectedResult: 3. Video stream remains in HD mode (threshold is exclusive: degrades only when bandwidth is strictly below 1.5 Mbps).

design_docs.name: Adaptive Bitrate Streaming Design
design_docs.description: Describes the adaptive bitrate (ABR) algorithm that monitors network bandwidth via WebRTC statistics and dynamically adjusts video encoding parameters. Documents the hysteresis logic that prevents rapid oscillation between HD and SD modes: degradation threshold at 1.5 Mbps (immediate), restoration threshold at 2.0 Mbps (with 10-second stabilization timer).

design_docs.name: WebRTC Video Encoder Interface Design
design_docs.description: Specifies the interface to the WebRTC video encoder, including the API calls to adjust resolution (setParameters), the supported resolution profiles (HD: 1280x720, SD: 640x480), and the bitrate constraints for each profile.

design_docs.name: Bandwidth Monitoring Detailed Design
design_docs.description: Detailed design of the bandwidth monitoring service that polls WebRTC getStats() API every 1 second, calculates the rolling average bandwidth over the last 5 seconds, and triggers quality adjustment events when thresholds are crossed. Documents the 10-second stabilization timer implementation that prevents premature HD restoration.
